fields.title: What is Django
fields.content: Django is a high-level Python web framework that encourages rapid development.

fields.title: Installing Django
fields.content: Install Django with pip: pip install django. Then create a project with django-admin startproject.

fields.title: Your First Model
fields.content: Models are Python classes that map to database tables. Each attribute is a field.

fields.title: Migrations Explained
fields.content: Migrations are Django's way of propagating changes to your models into the database schema.

fields.title: Function Views
fields.content: A view is a Python function that takes a web request and returns a web response.

fields.title: Template Basics
fields.content: Templates are HTML files with special tags that Django renders with context data.

fields.title: Understanding Decorators
fields.content: A decorator is a function that takes another function and extends its behavior.

fields.title: Generator Functions
fields.content: Generators produce values lazily using the yield keyword instead of returning a list.

fields.title: Variables and Types
fields.content: Python is dynamically typed. Variables are names bound to objects.

fields.title: If Statements
fields.content: Conditional execution with if, elif, else. Indentation defines blocks in Python.

fields.title: Client and Server
fields.content: The client sends a request, the server responds. HTTP is the protocol between them.

fields.title: HTTP Methods
fields.content: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE — each method has a semantic meaning in HTTP.

fields.title: Tags and Elements
fields.content: HTML documents are built from nested elements, each defined by tags.

fields.title: Tables and Rows
fields.content: Relational databases store data in tables with rows and columns.

fields.title: Primary and Foreign Keys
fields.content: Primary keys uniquely identify rows. Foreign keys link rows across tables.

fields.title: SELECT Statements
fields.content: SELECT retrieves data from one or more tables. WHERE filters rows.

fields.title: JOIN Operations
fields.content: JOIN combines rows from two tables based on a related column.

fields.title: Git Init and Commit
fields.content: git init creates a repository. git commit saves a snapshot of your changes.

fields.title: Viewing History
fields.content: git log shows commit history. git diff shows changes between commits.

fields.title: Creating Branches
fields.content: git branch creates a branch. git checkout switches between branches.

fields.title: Resources and URIs
fields.content: REST models everything as a resource, identified by a URI.

fields.title: Stateless Requests
fields.content: Each request contains all information needed to process it — no session state.

fields.title: 2xx and 4xx Codes
fields.content: 2xx means success. 4xx means client error (e.g. 404 Not Found, 400 Bad Request).

fields.title: Writing Your First Test
fields.content: A test is a function that asserts behavior. Use assert to check expected results.

fields.title: Mocks and Patches
fields.content: Mocks replace real objects in tests to isolate behavior and avoid side effects.

fields.title: ls, cd, pwd
fields.content: ls lists files. cd changes directory. pwd prints the current directory.

fields.title: File Permissions
fields.content: chmod changes file mode. chown changes owner. Permissions are rwx for user/group/other.

fields.title: The Pipe Operator
fields.content: The | operator sends stdout of one command to stdin of another.

fields.title: Environment Variables
fields.content: Environment variables configure apps without changing code. Use os.environ in Python.

fields.title: Continuous Integration
fields.content: CI runs tests automatically on every push. Catches regressions early.
